main.title: Street Fighter V
main.subtitle: The Fighting Game as an Evolving Platform
main.summary: Street Fighter V arrived in 2016 with a new way to distinguish its fighters.

cards.heading: A different set of tools
cards.text: Street Fighter V arrived in 2016 with a new way to distinguish its fighters. The V-System gave each character an individual skill and a trigger ability. Familiar attacks still depended on distance and timing, but a shared pair of button commands could produce very different decisions from one fighter to the next.

cards.heading: One command, different answers
cards.text: A V-Skill could help with movement, defence or offence without spending the V-Gauge. Ryu's skill, for example, allowed a timed parry. The point was not to give everyone the same defensive technique: the differences made learning the opponent's character important alongside learning one's own.

cards.heading: Spend the gauge
cards.text: V-Trigger spends a filled V-Gauge on a character-specific effect, while V-Reversal offers a way to interrupt pressure during a block. A separate EX Gauge powers enhanced special moves and Critical Arts. The match becomes a sequence of small exchanges that also changes which larger responses remain available.

main.title: Stardew Valley
main.subtitle: A New Life, One Day at a Time
main.summary: Stardew Valley is a 2016 farm life simulation video game developed by Eric "ConcernedApe" Barone.

cards.heading: Inherit a farm, choose a life
cards.text: Stardew Valley is a 2016 farm life simulation video game developed by Eric "ConcernedApe" Barone. Players take the role of a character who inherits their deceased grandfather's dilapidated farm. The game is open-ended, with players managing the farm by clearing land, growing seasonal crops, and raising animals. Players can acquire skills in farming, foraging, fishing, mining, and combat. Social features include building relationships with townspeople, with the option to marry and have a child. A later update added multiplayer, allowing online play with others.

cards.heading: Four years to build a valley
cards.text: Barone created Stardew Valley by himself over four years as an indie developer. He began the project to improve his programming and game design skills. He was heavily inspired by the Harvest Moon series (now named Story of Seasons), with additions to address some of those games' shortcomings. British studio Chucklefish approached Barone halfway through development with an offer to publish the game, allowing him to focus on completing it. It was released for Windows in February 2016 before being ported to several other platforms.

cards.heading: A success cultivated over time
cards.text: Stardew Valley received generally positive reviews from critics, including Yasuhiro Wada, the creator of Harvest Moon. The game has been cited as one of the best video games ever made and is credited with causing a resurgence in popularity for the farming sim genre. It became one of the best-selling video games, selling 50 million copies by February 2026. The game appeared on several publications' year-end lists and received accolades, including the Breakthrough Award at the Golden Joystick Awards and a nomination for Best Game at the British Academy Games Awards.

cards.heading: Planting before the season ends
cards.text: Crops take different numbers of days to grow, and each season has an end. Players must leave enough time to harvest what they plant. Planning the field means comparing a crop?s growing time with the days remaining.

cards.heading: Learning what neighbours like
cards.text: Townspeople have individual preferences for gifts. Learning those tastes gives crops and collected objects another use alongside selling them. Regular visits and suitable presents help the player develop relationships around the village.

main.title: Clash Royale
main.subtitle: An Arena in the Palm of Your Hand
main.summary: Clash Royale is a 2016 real-time strategy mobile game developed and published by Supercell.

cards.heading: Cards and Towers in Real Time
cards.text: Clash Royale is a 2016 real-time strategy mobile game developed and published by Supercell. It combines elements of collectible card games, tower defense, and multiplayer online battle arena (MOBA). Players collect cards and create a deck to use in 3–5 minute battles, with the aim to destroy opposing towers whilst defending their own. Released worldwide on March 2, 2016, the game is the first spin-off of Clash of Clans, another title developed by Supercell.

cards.heading: Strategy Designed for Portrait Screens
cards.text: With development beginning in 2014, Clash Royale shifted towards gaming on vertical phone screens (as opposed to tablets) and real-time gameplay compared to Clash of Clans. It uses a free-to-play monetization model, including microtransactions and artificial scarcity of in-game resources. From July 2019, it features monthly seasons, which coincide with regular content updates and a monthly battle pass called “Pass Royale”.

cards.heading: Short Matches, a Contested Economy
cards.text: Clash Royale received favorable reviews from critics when it was first released, with reviewers citing the game's quick, short matches and its depth of strategy. Matchmaking received mixed reviews. It has also been referred to as a "pay-to-win" game and has drawn criticism for its monetization techniques.

main.title: Dark Souls III
main.subtitle: The Last Ember
main.summary: Dark Souls III is a 2016 action role-playing game developed by FromSoftware, which published it in Japan, with Bandai Namco Entertainment publishing it internationally.

cards.heading: Returning to the First Flame
cards.text: Dark Souls III is a 2016 action role-playing game developed by FromSoftware, which published it in Japan, with Bandai Namco Entertainment publishing it internationally. Released for the PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and Windows, it is the third and final entry in the Dark Souls trilogy. The game follows the Ashen One, an unkindled warrior, on a quest involving the Lords of Cinder and the fading First Flame. It is played from a third-person perspective, and players use weapons, armour, magic, shields, and consumables to fight enemies. Series creator Hidetaka Miyazaki returned as a director after having a supervisory role on Dark Souls II.

cards.heading: The Legacy of Ash
cards.text: Dark Souls III received generally positive reviews and was commercially successful, with critics describing it as a fitting conclusion to the series. It shipped over three million copies by May 2016 and had surpassed 10 million in sales by May 2020. It won several awards, including Ultimate Game of the Year at the 2016 Golden Joystick Awards and Role-Playing/Massively Multiplayer Game of the Year at the 20th Annual D.I.C.E. Awards. Two downloadable content expansions, Ashes of Ariandel and The Ringed City, were released in 2016 and 2017, respectively. A compilation version, Dark Souls III: The Fire Fades Edition, containing the base game and both expansions, was released in April 2017.

main.title: Hyper Light Drifter
main.subtitle: Ruins to Read, a Life to Save
main.summary: A sick traveller searches the ruins of Hyper Light Drifter for knowledge that might save them.

cards.heading: A Journey Against Time
cards.text: A sick traveller searches the ruins of Hyper Light Drifter for knowledge that might save them. Heart Machine released the game for computers on 31 March 2016. Broken machines and unfamiliar monuments suggest a history that the player must piece together, while the Drifter has an urgent reason to keep moving.

cards.heading: A World That Speaks in Images
cards.text: Alex Preston described a deliberate move away from long explanations: encounters and conversations would communicate through images. Landmarks, colour and animation carry information that another game might put into dialogue. The player reads a place by crossing it, noticing what survived and what remains dangerous.

cards.heading: The Beauty of Unease
cards.text: Combat brings a different kind of attention. Enemies react visibly to blows, and groups require more than repeating an attack against a passive target. Disasterpeace, the composer Rich Vreeland, supplies an uneasy musical atmosphere. Exploration can feel quiet without becoming safe; the ruins remain beautiful places to be afraid in.

cards.heading: A Deeply Personal Story
cards.text: Alx Preston drew on his experience of congenital heart disease and repeated hospital stays when imagining the Drifter's illness. He had already used painting and film to express encounters with fragile health. Making a game offered another way to share those feelings while building the exploration and strategic combat he admired in A Link to the Past and Diablo. Years working as an animator helped him begin the project in 2013. The protagonist's terminal condition makes that personal history part of the journey, giving the search through a dangerous world a vulnerability beyond the combat itself.

main.title: Alienation
main.subtitle: Classes and loot in a twin-stick battle
main.summary: Alienation combines Housemarque?s twin-stick shooting with character classes, loot and four-player online cooperation.

cards.heading: Arcade shooting with lasting upgrades
cards.text: Alienation is Housemarque?s 2016 PlayStation 4 shooter, released on April 26. Players move and aim through alien swarms using twin-stick controls, while classes, weapon statistics and upgrades shape their character?s abilities. Online cooperation supports up to four players.

cards.heading: Three classes in a squad
cards.text: Bio-Specialist, Tank and Saboteur offer different offensive, defensive and support abilities. Positioning depends on what teammates can provide as well as where enemies are moving. Each class gives the squad another set of options.

cards.heading: Finding and upgrading weapons
cards.text: Weapons and modifiers vary in rarity and statistics. Upgrades encourage players to repeat missions and try different combinations. During a fight, stronger equipment still needs to be supported by dodging projectiles and managing space.

cards.heading: Keeping room to move
cards.text: Large enemy groups and projectiles can fill an arena quickly. Teams need room to escape while remaining close enough to help one another. Colour, direction and timing help distinguish threats during the busiest fights.

main.title: Kirby: Planet Robobot
main.subtitle: HAL Laboratory · Nintendo 3DS
main.summary: Kirby: Planet Robobot is HAL Laboratory's Nintendo 3DS platform adventure about an invasion that turns Planet Popstar into machinery. The Haltmann Works Company is stripping the world of its resources, and Kirby sets out through landscapes increasingly occupied by pipes, factories and mechanical enemies. His familiar inhaling and Copy Abilities remain useful, but a stolen suit of Robobot Armor gives him another scale of strength. A large machine becomes something to pilot, allowing Kirby to turn the invaders' equipment against the structures they have built.

cards.heading: Popstar becomes a factory
cards.text: Kirby: Planet Robobot is HAL Laboratory's Nintendo 3DS platform adventure about an invasion that turns Planet Popstar into machinery. The Haltmann Works Company is stripping the world of its resources, and Kirby sets out through landscapes increasingly occupied by pipes, factories and mechanical enemies. His familiar inhaling and Copy Abilities remain useful, but a stolen suit of Robobot Armor gives him another scale of strength. A large machine becomes something to pilot, allowing Kirby to turn the invaders' equipment against the structures they have built.

cards.heading: A copied power changes the machine
cards.text: The armor scans enemies and transforms to match their abilities. A sword produces mechanical blades, while other forms provide different ways to cross a stage or attack its obstacles. Its size lets Kirby shift objects that would otherwise remain fixed in place. The routes use these changes for small puzzles as well as battles, asking the player to notice where the current form might fit. Leaving the suit returns attention to Kirby's ordinary movements, giving each change in scale a practical purpose.

cards.heading: A familiar world viewed through machinery
cards.text: Stages move between foreground and background routes, using the 3DS display to make one layer interact with another. Code Cubes hidden along the way reward a more thorough search. Separate activities include the cooperative Team Kirby Clash and the small three-dimensional arenas of Kirby 3D Rumble. Hirokazu Ando and Jun Ishikawa's music accompanies a campaign that lets industrial scenery intrude on the series' bright landscapes. The contrast grows increasingly pointed as Kirby approaches the company directing the transformation of his home.

main.title: Stellaris
main.subtitle: A Galaxy to Discover and Build
main.summary: Stellaris is Paradox?s 2016 space strategy game, combining exploration, diplomacy and the administration of a player-created civilisation.

cards.heading: Paradox takes strategy into space
cards.text: Stellaris is Paradox Development Studio?s space strategy game, released on May 9, 2016. Players guide a civilisation through a procedurally generated galaxy, exploring stars, negotiating with neighbours and managing an expanding empire. A campaign combines early discovery with longer-term political and economic decisions.

cards.heading: Surveying an unknown galaxy
cards.text: Ships survey star systems, investigate anomalies and make first contact with other species. The generated galaxy begins largely unknown. Exploration reveals the resources and neighbours around which an empire can plan its expansion.

cards.heading: Choosing a civilisation?s rules
cards.text: Ethics, authority and species traits shape the player?s civilisation. Later updates expanded the options: civics and hive minds arrived in 2017 through the Banks update and Utopia expansion. Different societies bring different needs and diplomatic possibilities to a campaign.

cards.heading: An empire faces a crisis
cards.text: Endgame crises introduce major threats after borders and alliances have become established. Responding can force rivals to change priorities or work together. The same star systems and routes built up over the campaign become resources to defend.

main.title: Uncharted 4: A Thief's End
main.subtitle: Nathan Drake?s last treasure hunt
main.summary: Uncharted 4 closes Nathan Drake?s story with large set pieces, wider areas to explore and a closer view of life beyond adventure.

cards.heading: The end of Nathan?s journey
cards.text: Uncharted 4: A Thief?s End is Naughty Dog?s 2016 PlayStation 4 adventure, released on May 10. It closes Nathan Drake?s story with familiar climbing, combat and large set pieces, while wider areas and quieter scenes give the characters more time together.

cards.heading: Life outside the adventure
cards.text: Nathan?s relationships and promises outside treasure hunting become central to the story. Domestic moments and conversations between action sequences show the life he risks returning to adventure. Naughty Dog described the challenge of concluding his journey as part of an unusually large production.

cards.heading: Exploring wider routes
cards.text: Madagascar and other wider sections give players several routes towards set destinations. A jeep allows stops to inspect ruins, while conversations continue during travel. These spaces offer more freedom within the series? directed adventure.

cards.heading: Climbing and fighting with the rope
cards.text: The rope connects climbing, swinging and combat. Position, momentum and the chosen anchor affect a swing. Nathan can use it to cross gaps, recover from falls or move quickly into and out of enemy positions.

main.title: Doom
main.subtitle: Hell returns at full speed
main.summary: Doom is a 2016 first-person shooter game developed by id Software and published by Bethesda Softworks.

cards.heading: From Mars to Hell: Doom returns
cards.text: Doom is a 2016 first-person shooter game developed by id Software and published by Bethesda Softworks. The game is the first major installment in the Doom series since 2004's Doom 3 and is a reboot of the franchise. It was released for PlayStation 4, Windows, and Xbox One in May 2016. A port for Nintendo Switch was co-developed with Panic Button and released in November 2017, and a version for Stadia was released in August 2020. Players take the role of an ancient warrior, known colloquially as the Doom Slayer, as he battles demonic forces within an energy-mining facility on Mars and in Hell.

cards.heading: From Doom 4 to a fresh start
cards.text: The game was announced as Doom 4 in 2008, and that version underwent an extensive development cycle with different builds and designs before the game was restarted in 2011 and re-revealed as simply Doom in 2014. It was tested by customers who pre-ordered the 2014 MachineGames game Wolfenstein: The New Order and the general public. Mick Gordon composed the music, with contributions by Richard Devine. The game also has an online multiplayer component and a level editor known as "SnapMap", co-developed with Certain Affinity and Escalation Studios respectively.

cards.heading: Reception, sales and new chapters
cards.text: Doom was well received by critics and players. The single-player campaign, graphics, soundtrack, and gameplay received considerable praise, whereas the multiplayer mode drew significant criticism. It ranked second in United States retail unit sales for May 2016 and debuted at number two in the United Kingdom retail charts. SteamSpy estimated more than 500,000 PC owners by the end of that month. A sequel, Doom Eternal, was released in March 2020. A prequel, Doom: The Dark Ages, was released in May 2025.
